title.en: Electron transport system and oxidative phosphorylation
title.kn: ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಸಾಗಣೆ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಮತ್ತು ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಣ ಫಾಸ್ಫೊರಿಲೀಕರಣ

heading.en: Where the oxygen we breathe ends up

hook.en: All the NADH and FADH₂ made so far are like charged batteries. In the inner mitochondrial membrane, their electrons flow to oxygen, and the energy released makes most of the cell's ATP.
hook.kn: ಇದುವರೆಗೆ ಉಂಟಾದ NADH ಮತ್ತು FADH₂ ಚಾರ್ಜ್ ಆದ ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿಗಳಂತೆ. ಮೈಟೋಕಾಂಡ್ರಿಯದ ಒಳಪೊರೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅವುಗಳ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳು ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕದತ್ತ ಹರಿದು, ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯಾದ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ATP ತಯಾರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

objectives.en: Name the complexes of the ETS and their order.
Explain the role of oxygen as the final acceptor.

narration.en: All the NADH and FADH₂ made so far are like charged batteries. In the inner mitochondrial membrane, their electrons flow to oxygen, and the energy released makes most of the cell's ATP.
narration.kn: ಇದುವರೆಗೆ ಉಂಟಾದ NADH ಮತ್ತು FADH₂ ಚಾರ್ಜ್ ಆದ ಬ್ಯಾಟರಿಗಳಂತೆ. ಮೈಟೋಕಾಂಡ್ರಿಯದ ಒಳಪೊರೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅವುಗಳ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳು ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕದತ್ತ ಹರಿದು, ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯಾದ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ATP ತಯಾರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: The ETS is located in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Electrons from NADH produced in the matrix are oxidised by NADH dehydrogenase (complex I) and transferred to ubiquinone. FADH₂ from the Krebs cycle passes its electrons to ubiquinone through complex II. Reduced ubiquinone (ubiquinol) is oxidised by cytochrome bc₁ complex (complex III). Cytochrome c, a small protein attached to the outer surface of the inner membrane, is a mobile carrier between complex III and complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase, containing cytochromes a and a₃ and two copper centres). Oxygen is the final hydrogen acceptor: it accepts electrons and protons and forms water. Unlike photophosphorylation, where light energy drives the proton gradient, here the energy comes from oxidation–reduction; hence oxidative phosphorylation.

points.en: Order: Complex I → ubiquinone → Complex III → cytochrome c → Complex IV → O₂.
O₂ is the final acceptor; water is formed.

narration.kn: ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಸಾಗಣೆ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಮೈಟೋಕಾಂಡ್ರಿಯದ ಒಳಪೊರೆಯಲ್ಲಿದೆ. ಸಂಕೀರ್ಣ I ರಿಂದ IV ವರೆಗೆ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳು ಸಾಗಿ ಕೊನೆಗೆ ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕ ಅವನ್ನು ಸ್ವೀಕರಿಸಿ ನೀರು ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Let us draw the inner mitochondrial membrane and pass electrons along it to oxygen.

say.en: The complexes sit in the inner mitochondrial membrane. NADH hands its electrons to complex I; FADH₂ enters through complex II.
Electrons pass from complex I to ubiquinone, complex III, cytochrome c and complex IV. On the way protons are pumped out.
Oxygen is the final electron acceptor at complex IV. It takes the electrons and protons and becomes water.
Protons flow back into the matrix through ATP synthase, complex V. F₀ is the channel; F₁ is the head that makes ATP.
Each NADH gives 3 ATP and each FADH₂ gives 2 ATP. Without oxygen the whole chain stops.

body.en: The energy of electron transfer is used by ATP synthase (complex V) to make ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. It has two major parts: F₁, a peripheral headpiece that contains the site for ATP synthesis, and F₀, an integral membrane protein complex forming the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane. For each ATP produced, 2 H⁺ pass through F₀ from the intermembrane space to the matrix down the electrochemical proton gradient. The oxidation of one NADH gives rise to 3 ATP, while that of one FADH₂ produces 2 ATP.

points.en: F₀: proton channel in the membrane; F₁: headpiece where ATP is made.
Protons flow from intermembrane space to matrix.

problem.en: From the link reaction and the Krebs cycle, one glucose yields 8 NADH and 2 FADH₂. How many ATP do these give in the ETS?

steps.en: Total from the ETS for these carriers = 24 + 4 = 28 ATP.
